S1.text:
Declaration of Intent. Raise Jira Ticket on DP Demand Board. Create a single source of truth to log the demand and kick-off triage.. Step 1: Check for existing/duplicate tickets using keywords and stakeholdersâ€™ names.
Step 2: Select the correct Demand Board project and issue type (e.g., Demand/Initiative).
Step 3: Enter a clear Summary using the pattern: <Product/Change> â€“ <Outcome> â€“ <Domain>.
Step 4: Fill Description with problem statement, desired business outcomes, scope in/out, key risks, and high-level timeline.
Step 5: Populate custom fields: domain, sponsoring area, product owner, tech lead, data owner, target environment(s).
Step 6: Add labels/tags (e.g., data-product, privacy, security, customer-impact) for filtering and dashboards.
Step 7: Link related tickets (defects, dependencies, epics) and any portfolio initiatives.
Step 8: Attach supporting artefacts (early notes, diagrams) and grant appropriate permissions/watchers.
Step 9: Save and capture the Jira key; share the link with stakeholders.
Step 10: Set the status to 'Intake' (or equivalent) to trigger triage workflow and notifications.

S2.text:
Declaration of Intent. Complete Declaration of Intent (DOI) Form. Document the early concept, value case, and data needs in a standard format.. Step 1: Download/open the latest DOI template and confirm version from the governance space.
Step 2: Check Data-Product Naming Standard, each specific for ODP,FCP,CDP.
Step 3: Store the signed-off DOI in the repository and link it back to Jira.

S3.text:
Declaration of Intent. Present to Data Products Working Group (DPWG). Obtain early peer review on feasibility, reuse, and standards alignment.. Step 1: Book a DPWG slot and share pre-read (DOI + 6â€“8 slide deck) 48 hours in advance.
Step 2: Prepare deck covering: problem, value, scope, data domains, privacy/security flags, reuse, delivery plan.
Step 3: Include a simple scorecard (complexity, risk, reuse potential) to focus discussion.
Step 4: Present the proposal (10 minutes) and walk through decisions needed from the group.
Step 5: Capture questions, actions, and decisions live in the meeting notes.
Step 6: Update the DOI and Jira with outcomes (proceed/refine/park) and named owners for actions.
Step 7: Share the updated artefacts and confirm next forum/date (e.g., DPC/ARC).

S4.text:
Declaration of Intent. Present to Data Products Chapter (DPC). Secure chapter alignment on ownership, capacity, and ways of working.. Step 1: Book DPC agenda time; circulate DPWG outcome and updated DOI.
Step 2: Confirm product ownership and core roles; propose RACI.
Step 3: Review capacity and tentative sprint plan; identify staffing gaps.
Step 4: Align on tooling, environments, and definition of ready/done for increments.
Step 5: Validate dependencies across squads/chapters and agree integration points.
Step 6: Record chapter endorsement, conditions, and date to re-confirm if anything changes.
Step 7: Update Jira and the catalogue entry with ownership and delivery cadence.

S5.text:
Declaration of Intent. Endorsement by Data Architecture Review Committee (Data ARC). Gain architectural endorsement against enterprise and data standards.. Step 1: Prepare an architecture overview (context, C4/system diagrams, data flows, integrations).
Step 2: Map to reference architectures and platform standards; call out reuse and deviations.
Step 3: Summarise non-functional requirements and how they are met (availability, resilience, performance).
Step 4: Highlight security, privacy, data quality, and lineage controls embedded in the design.
Step 5: Attend a pre-ARC clinic to test the narrative and capture pre-work actions.
Step 6: Present at ARC; seek endorsement with conditions and record actions/owners/dates.
Step 7: Update the solution pack and Jira with outcomes; track closure of any conditions.

S6.text:
Declaration of Intent. Data Product Catalogue Metadata. Register the concept so it is discoverable and governed from day one.. Step 1: Open the catalogue and create a new product entry linked to the Jira key.
Step 2: Populate mandatory fields: name, description, domain, owners (product/data/tech), and contacts.
Step 3: Add classifications, intended consumers, SLAs/SLOs, and expected availability.
Step 4: Register initial datasets, interfaces/APIs, and lineage seeds (producers/consumers).
Step 5: Record quality metrics and thresholds, retention rules, and recovery objectives.
Step 6: Validate against required field rules; fix warnings; submit for publish.
Step 7: Share the catalogue link in Jira and with DPWG/DPC; schedule periodic metadata refresh.

S7.text:
Solution Record. Complete Your Change Kick Off Form & Raise Solution Record. Formally initiate the change and create the master solution record.. Step 1: Open the change portal and select 'New Solution Record'.
Step 2: Enter scope, objectives, environments (dev/test/prod), and dependencies.
Step 3: Define non-functional requirements and acceptance criteria.
Step 4: Document deployment plan, rollback/contingency, and back-out triggers.
Step 5: Identify approval forums (security, privacy, service) and attach the DOI/ARC pack.
Step 6: Assign owners and due dates for downstream assessments.
Step 7: Submit for registration and capture the solution record ID; link to Jira.

S8.text:
Solution Record. E2E Cloud Control Assurance. Evidence cloud controls and risk compliance for all components.. Step 1: Inventory cloud services (compute, storage, networking, databases, managed services).
Step 2: Map components to control domains (identity, encryption, logging, network, backup/DR, change).
Step 3: Complete assurance questionnaire and provide evidence (IaC templates, policies, configs).
Step 4: Attach vulnerability scans, CIS benchmarks, and key management procedures.
Step 5: Record exceptions/deviations with risk treatments and target closure dates.
Step 6: Submit to cloud assurance for review and resolve comments.
Step 7: Obtain sign-off and store the assurance report in the solution record.

S9.text:
Solution Record. E2E Customer Impacts (CSOC). Assess and mitigate any direct or indirect customer impacts.. Step 1: Identify customer-facing journeys, channels, and any potential outages.
Step 2: Assess impacts on SLAs, service windows, communications, and vulnerable customer considerations.
Step 3: Define mitigations and draft customer/colleague comms (where required).
Step 4: Validate monitoring and incident procedures for customer harm detection.
Step 5: Submit assessment to the oversight group and track actions to closure.
Step 6: Record the final decision and link comms plan in the solution record.

S10.text:
Solution Record. Records Management. Ensure records classification, retention, and disposition comply with policy.. Step 1: List records created/consumed by the change and map to record classes.
Step 2: Determine retention periods, legal holds, and triggers for disposition.
Step 3: Specify storage locations, access controls, and metadata capture requirements.
Step 4: Update retention schedules and catalogue entries accordingly.
Step 5: Evidence compliance (screenshots, policy mappings) and submit for review.
Step 6: Record approvals and link artefacts in the solution record.

S11.text:
Solution Record. E2E Service Provision Impact Assessment (SPIA). Validate operational readiness and service support impacts.. Step 1: Identify affected services and owning support groups.
Step 2: Define monitoring/alerting, logging, and capacity/performance baselines.
Step 3: Update runbooks, KBs, and on-call arrangements; confirm OLAs/SLAs.
Step 4: Assess operational risks and required tooling or access.
Step 5: Obtain acceptance from service owners and store evidence.
Step 6: Link SPIA outputs to the change and go-live checklist.

S12.text:
Solution Record. E2E Solution Design. Document the target end-to-end design for build and testing.. Step 1: Produce architecture and component diagrams with data flows and interfaces.
Step 2: Define schemas/contracts, API endpoints, and transformation/lineage mapping.
Step 3: Capture non-functional design (availability, resilience, performance, observability).
Step 4: Specify security, privacy, and data quality controls embedded in the design.
Step 5: Document error handling, recovery, and deployment strategy.
Step 6: Baseline the design after peer review and store in the solution record.

S13.text:
Solution Record. E2E Architecture. Review and approve the architecture against enterprise standards.. Step 1: Compile the architecture pack (diagrams, ADRs, standards mapping, trade-offs).
Step 2: Conduct internal review; address gaps and prepare FAQs.
Step 3: Present to the architecture board and walk through key decisions.
Step 4: Record approval/conditions and assign owners with due dates.
Step 5: Update the pack and the solution record; monitor closure of conditions.

S14.text:
Solution Record. Service Introduction. Confirm supportability and handover into live operations.. Step 1: Complete the service introduction checklist and identify gaps.
Step 2: Finalise support model, RACI, and escalation paths.
Step 3: Publish runbooks, KB articles, and training materials for support teams.
Step 4: Validate backup/restore, DR plans, and complete a DR test where required.
Step 5: Confirm monitoring dashboards and alert thresholds are in place.
Step 6: Obtain service acceptance and attach evidence to the solution record.

S15.text:
Solution Record. E2E Data Privacy (DPIA). Assess personal-data processing and record privacy risk treatment.. Step 1: Complete DPIA screening to confirm if a full DPIA is required.
Step 2: If required, document processing purposes, data categories, lawful basis, and data flows.
Step 3: Assess data minimisation, retention, transparency, and data subject rights enablement.
Step 4: Evaluate transfers (third parties/locations) and protective measures (e.g., pseudonymisation).
Step 5: Identify risks and agree mitigations; record residual risk and owners.
Step 6: Obtain privacy approval and store outputs in the solution record.

S16.text:
Solution Record. E2E Information Security. Confirm security requirements and control effectiveness.. Step 1: Perform threat/risk assessment and define control requirements.
Step 2: Evidence identity, access, key/secret management, and encryption controls.
Step 3: Provide secure SDLC artefacts (code scan, dependency checks, SAST/DAST results).
Step 4: Attach pen-test or security review outcomes and remediation plans.
Step 5: Record residual risks and obtain security approval.

S17.text:
Solution Record. Colleague Impacts (PSOC). Understand and plan for impacts to colleagues and internal users.. Step 1: Run a change impact assessment across affected roles and processes.
Step 2: Define training needs, SOP updates, and access/tooling changes.
Step 3: Draft internal communications and adoption plan with milestones.
Step 4: Validate business readiness criteria and measures of success.
Step 5: Obtain oversight acknowledgement/approval and store evidence.

S18.text:
Solution Record. Financial Crime. Evidence compliance with AML/sanctions requirements for the change.. Step 1: Confirm whether new or changed data/processes affect screening/monitoring.
Step 2: Validate KYC/KYB data availability and data quality for controls.
Step 3: Assess transaction monitoring, sanctions screening, and reporting implications.
Step 4: Agree control coverage/tuning changes and document testing needs.
Step 5: Obtain Financial Crime sign-off and archive evidence in the solution record.

S19.text:
Solution Record. CMA (Competition and Markets Authority). Confirm the change aligns with applicable CMA obligations.. Step 1: Identify potential impacts on fair outcomes, disclosures, and competition.
Step 2: Review relevant obligations (e.g., pricing transparency, switching) where applicable.
Step 3: Obtain legal/regulatory input on any edge cases or mitigations.
Step 4: Document the assessment, decisions, and any required controls.
Step 5: File the record in the solution repository and link to Jira.

S20.text:
Solution Record. E2E Group Model Impacts. Identify and govern any model changes or dependencies.. Step 1: Inventory affected models and their purposes/owners.
Step 2: Define input data changes, retraining needs, and validation approach.
Step 3: Register material changes with model governance and update documentation.
Step 4: Plan monitoring (stability, drift, performance) and alerting.
Step 5: Obtain required approvals prior to deployment and store evidence.

S21.text:
Solution Record. E2E Change Gateway. Aggregate evidence for a go/no-go decision across governance areas.. Step 1: Compile approvals from architecture, security, privacy, service, finance, and impact forums.
Step 2: Complete the readiness checklist (testing, monitoring, rollback, comms).
Step 3: Document risk acceptances and open actions with owners/dates.
Step 4: Present to the gateway forum; capture go/no-go decision and conditions.
Step 5: Publish decision notes and update the project schedule accordingly.

S22.text:
Solution Record. E2E Financial Reporting. Validate impacts to finance processes, GL, and regulatory reporting.. Step 1: Map data flows to finance systems and identify GL/reconciliation touchpoints.
Step 2: Confirm accounting treatments and materiality with finance controllers.
Step 3: Assess impacts on statutory and regulatory returns and control updates.
Step 4: Define testing and evidence required for SOX/ICFR as applicable.
Step 5: Obtain finance sign-off and link outputs in the solution record.
